title: Starting an LSP connection on 4.6 Beta 2 with NeoVim causes a segmentation fault when GDUnit4 is installed
body:
### Tested versions

Official builds
4.6-beta1 d743736f8 works
4.6-beta2 551ce8d47 segmentation fault

Local dev build 
551ce8d47 segmentation fault

GDUnit https://github.com/godot-gdunit-labs/gdUnit4/commit/c8d63a903b8be964b1564112abc18b95723bbb16

### System information

Godot v4.6.beta2 - Bazzite 43.20260101.0 (Kinoite) on Wayland - X11 display driver, Multi-window, 3 monitors - Vulkan (Forward+) - dedicated NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4090 (nvidia; 590.44.01) - 13th Gen Intel(R) Core(TM) i9-13900K (32 threads) - 125.5 GiB memory

### Issue description

To trigger this problem I have NeoVim running and I start Godot. Once Godot runs, I do `:LspStart` in NeoVim.  I see `[LSP] Connection Taken` in the editor log and then the editor becomes unresponsive. After a while I get `Segmentation fault         (core dumped)` in the terminal.

Doing `nc -z -w 1 127.0.0.1 6005` on the `dev build`, I get this in the editor log. I think this is to be expected.

```
[LSP] Connection Taken
[LSP] Disconnected
Socket error: 0.
Error when polling socket.
Socket error: 0.
Error when polling socket.
```

### Steps to reproduce

- Create a New Project
- Create a new GDScript file
- Add https://github.com/godot-gdunit-labs/gdUnit4/commit/c8d63a903b8be964b1564112abc18b95723bbb16 to your project
- Enable GDUnit in Project Settings
- Connect LSP

Disable GDUnit, close editor, remove GDUnit, start editor and LSP works again.

N/A
